sheet-27.description: A new sheet of September 1923, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the northern part of Fairview. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. The built-up grid lies between Kamena Street and Cliff Street, crossed by the numbered streets from 4th to 10th, with Anderson Avenue along the bottom edge and Bergen Boulevard running diagonally across the upper part of the sheet from the lower left towards the upper right. Westview Place runs between Bergen Boulevard and 9th Street. West of Kamena Street a second, more thinly built grid is laid out along Broad, Roosevelt, Murray and McKinley (printed without a suffix) between 8th Street and Anderson Avenue. The blocks are subdivided into narrow house lots and carry the large spaced lettering of the subdivision maps they were sold under. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings, with brick stores and dwellings concentrated near Anderson Avenue, where St. John the Baptist's Roman Catholic church and school stand between Kamena and Walker Streets. Scattered small industrial and commercial premises appear along the grid, among them a feather factory, an embroidery factory, a wagon house, a bakery and a garage, and the Fairview hook and ladder company No. 3 on Walker at 4th Street. The upper left of the sheet, beyond Bergen Boulevard, is open land with only a few buildings, including a dance hall near Fairview Avenue (Bulls Ferry Road), which crosses the top left corner. Water pipes are shown along the streets, with fire hydrants at many corners. Block numbers run from 2 to 17 east of Kamena Street and from 4 to 10 and 601 to 603 west of it.
notes: Broad west of Kamena is Kennedy Drive in OpenStreetMap; Roosevelt and Mc Kinley are Roosevelt Street and McKinley Street; Murray lies about on the line of today's Delano Place; Kamena, Walker and Cliff are Kamena Street, Walker Street and Cliff Street.
Bergen Boulevard was left out of the control: the modern road does not follow the drawn alignment across the upper left of the sheet.
Printed as New Sheet, Sept. 1923; part of this territory was formerly shown on Sheets 29 and 30 and old Sheets 27 and 28.

Fairview, Sheet 27 (new sheet Sept. 1923), 100 ft. Kamena, Westview Pl, Walker, Cliff, 4th-10th St, Anderson Av, Bergen Blvd (diagonal), Broad Av (now Kennedy Drive), Roosevelt, Murray, McKinley. One part. Bergen Blvd left out (modern alignment differs).

sheet-28.description: A new sheet of September 1923, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the part of Fairview and Ridgefield east of Cliff Street. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. Cliff, Jersey Avenue, Morningside Avenue and Park Avenue run down the page from Bergen Boulevard at the top to Anderson Avenue at the bottom, crossed by 10th, 9th, 8th and 7th Streets; Sunset Terrace, Fairview Terrace and Ridgefield Terrace run between Bergen Boulevard and 10th Street, and Edgewater Avenue forms the right edge. The blocks are subdivided into narrow house lots lettered as Cliffside Park Realty Company Map No. 3 and No. 4, and the Ridgefield and Cliffside Park boundary line crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, while the Fairview and Ridgefield boundary runs down its left part. Buildings are scattered frame dwellings, densest along Park Avenue and in the lower left, where Public School No. 3 stands near Cliff. The lower right quarter is taken up by a large open block holding the Hackensack Water Company's reservoir, with a capacity of 25 million gallons, drawn as a rectangular basin. Water pipes of six to sixteen inches are drawn along the streets, including a sixteen-inch main along Edgewater Avenue. Most lots south of 7th Street are vacant and long and narrow, running back from the avenues.
notes: Edgewater Avenue is Edgewater Road in OpenStreetMap; Cliff is Cliff Street; 8th Street at Park Avenue and Edgewater Road is tagged North 8th Street.
Sunset, Fairview and Ridgefield Terraces gave no usable junctions with the listed streets.
Anderson Avenue is drawn about 32 ft wide against a right-of-way of about 67 ft today; its junctions were kept (residuals 1.6 to 3.3 m).
Printed as New Sheet, Sept. 1923; part of this territory was formerly shown on old sheet No. 27.

Fairview and Ridgefield, Sheet 28, 100 ft. Cliff, Jersey, Morningside, Park Av, Sunset/Fairview/Ridgefield Ter, Edgewater Av (now Edgewater Road), 7th-10th St, Bergen Blvd, Anderson Av; Hackensack Water Co reservoir. One part.

sheet-61.description: A new sheet of September 1923 covering a thinly built tract in Fort Lee, drawn at the larger scale of 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. Anderson Avenue runs along the top, with the stubs of Main Avenue, North Avenue and Centre Street beyond it, and Gerome (Eickhoff) Avenue along the bottom. Central (Centre) Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet. Mc Loud Drive, Slocum Way and Tom Hunter Road run down the page between Anderson and Gerome Avenues, and Whitman forms the right edge. The blocks west of Tom Hunter Road are cut into long rows of narrow numbered lots, almost all vacant, with only a handful of buildings near Anderson Avenue. East of Tom Hunter Road the large block 21 1/2 holds a few frame dwellings along Anderson Avenue and along its west side, with sheds and outbuildings, and most of it is open ground. South of Central Avenue the large block 20 contains a hotel lettered Cellas Park Hotel and a dance hall with related buildings near Whitman, while the blocks to the west are again rows of empty lots. A street right of way is lettered diagonally across the lower right corner. A twelve-inch water pipe is drawn along Anderson Avenue. The sheet is mostly a record of a subdivision laid out ahead of building.
notes: Drawn at 50 ft to an inch (fitted 8.03 px/ft), unlike the 100 ft sheets around it.
Central (Centre) Avenue is Center Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Mc Loud Drive is McCloud Drive; Whitman is Whiteman Street.
Central Avenue is drawn about 31 ft wide against a right-of-way of about 60 ft today.
Anderson Avenue / Mc Loud Drive was rejected (9.8 m from the fit).

Fort Lee, Sheet 61, 50 ft to an inch (fitted 8.0 px/ft). Anderson Av, Central (Centre) Av (now Center Avenue), Gerome (Eickhoff) Av, McLoud Drive, Slocum Way, Tom Hunter Rd, Whitman (now Whiteman Street). Mostly unbuilt lots. One part.

sheet-72.description: A new sheet of September 1923, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the centre of Leonia between the railroad and Broad Avenue. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. The Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) crosses the top of the sheet, with H. S. Ferndon's coal yard and building materials yard beside it at the corner of Central Avenue and Willow, including coal sheds, an auto and wagon shed and a gasoline station. Central Avenue runs down the left edge, with Spring Street and Romaine Place leading off it. Grand Avenue crosses the upper middle of the sheet and Broad Avenue the bottom; between them run Leonia Avenue, Woods Terrace, Coover and Kingsley, with Woodridge Place, Schor Avenue, Hillside Avenue, Cottage Place and Harrison running across them, and the stubs of Woodland Avenue and Harold Avenue below Broad Avenue. A Public Service right of way is lettered across the open block north of Grand Avenue. Large blocks 20 to 23 near the centre are only partly subdivided and hold scattered frame dwellings on large lots. The eastern blocks between Hillside Avenue and Harrison are closely built with dwellings, and a Roman Catholic church stands at Kingsley and Harrison. A church stands near Woodridge Place, and a row of brick stores lines Broad Avenue at Hillside Avenue. Water pipes, including a twenty-four inch main along Grand Avenue, are drawn along the streets.
notes: Coover, Kingsley, Harrison and Willow are Coover Street, Kingsley Street, Harrison Street and Willow Street in OpenStreetMap.
Broad Avenue / Hillside Avenue was rejected (19.8 m from the fit): Hillside Avenue does not meet Broad Avenue on its modern line here.
Woods Terrace is not in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad at the top is lettered N. R. R. of N. J. (Erie).

Leonia, Sheet 72, 100 ft. Grand Av, Broad Av, Leonia Av, Woodridge Pl, Woods Terrace, Hillside Av, Cottage Pl, Harrison, Coover, Kingsley, Schor Av, Central Av, Willow; railroad along the top. One part.

sheet-79.description: This additional sheet, dated September 1923 and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the central grid of Palisades Park between Castle Hill and Fairmount Avenues at the top and 11th Street at the bottom, and between Homestead Avenue and Palisades Boulevard. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. Four long avenues, Homestead, Brinkerhoff, Central Boulevard and Palisades Boulevard, run down the page, crossed by Glen Avenue and the numbered streets from 4th to 11th, which divide the area into regular blocks numbered 129 to 137, 98 to 106 and 71 to 79, each subdivided into narrow house lots of about 25 feet. Development is scattered and residential: most buildings are small frame dwellings with outbuildings and garages, with a few brick or tile buildings near 7th and 8th Streets and a group of stores at the corner of Central Boulevard and 11th Street. The Palisades Heights Fire Company building stands on 8th Street. Six-inch and twelve-inch water pipes are drawn along several streets, with fire hydrants at the corners. Along the left edge a narrow strip west of Homestead Avenue shows the ends of Abbott Avenue, Upland Place, Temple Terrace, Sunset Place, Rural Lane and Queensland Terrace, which curve away towards Northwood Way and Princeton Place; these blocks are numbered 155 to 162 and are drawn only in outline. Most of the lots are vacant, which gives the sheet the appearance of a newly laid out suburban tract rather than a built-up town.
notes: Homestead Avenue, Brinkerhoff Avenue, Central Boulevard and Palisades Boulevard carry an East prefix today (East Homestead Avenue, East Brinkerhoff Avenue, East Central Boulevard, East Palisades Boulevard).
Glen Avenue was left out of the control: two of its four junctions were 6 to 9 m from the fit.
Castle Hill Avenue and Fairmount Avenue, at the top edge, have no street of that name in OpenStreetMap today.
Printed as Additional Sheet, Sept. 1923.

Palisades Park, Sheet 79 (additional sheet Sept. 1923), 100 ft. Homestead, Brinkerhoff, Central Blvd, Palisades Blvd (now East ... prefixes), Castle Hill/Fairmount Av, Glen Av, 4th-11th St. One part. Glen Avenue left out (two of four junctions rejected at 6-9 m).

sheet-80.description: An additional sheet of September 1923, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, continuing sheet 79 southwards across the boundary between Palisades Park and Fort Lee, which is lettered along 14th Street. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper right. Homestead Avenue (south of the boundary Deerwood Avenue), Brinkerhoff Avenue, Central Avenue and Palisades Boulevard run down the page, crossed by the numbered streets from 11th to 19th; Anderson Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally. West of Brinkerhoff Avenue in Fort Lee the numbered streets give way to rounded blocks along Keswick Place, Juanita Place, Inwood Terrace, Harvard Terrace, Glen Road and Fairview Lane, and a narrow strip at the left edge shows the curving lots of Princeton Place, Overlook Place, Morningside Lane, Bergen Boulevard, Kingsland Lane and Jassamine Way west of Homestead and Deerwood Avenues. The Palisades Park blocks between 11th and 14th Streets are the most built up, with frame dwellings, some brick dwellings and stores, the Hill Top Hose Company No. 4 on 13th Street, and St. Nicholas Roman Catholic Church and rectory in the block between 13th and 14th Streets west of Brinkerhoff Avenue. Public School No. 4 with a school annex stands on Anderson Avenue between Brinkerhoff and Central Avenues. South of 14th Street the Fort Lee blocks are almost wholly vacant lots. In the lower right a street marked Not Named runs from 17th Street to Anderson Avenue, with large unsubdivided blocks 607 to 609, Euclid Road and Drury Lane beyond. Twelve-inch water mains run along Anderson Avenue and Central Avenue.
notes: 17th, 18th and 19th Streets east of Brinkerhoff Avenue are today Inwood Terrace, Harvard Place and Glen Road, continuing the streets of those names west of it; Harvard Terrace is Harvard Place.

Deerwood Avenue is Deerwood Road; north of 14th Street Homestead Avenue and Brinkerhoff Avenue are East Homestead Avenue and East Brinkerhoff Avenue, and Central Avenue is East Central Boulevard north of 14th Street and Central Boulevard south of it.
Central Avenue was left out of the control: all its junctions were 3 to 4 m from the fit of the other streets.
A street lettered Not Named runs between 17th Street and Anderson Avenue east of Central Avenue.
Bergen Boulevard today cuts diagonally across the blocks between Homestead and Brinkerhoff Avenues north of 14th Street; it is not drawn there.

Palisades Park and Fort Lee, Sheet 80, 100 ft. Homestead/Deerwood Av, Brinkerhoff, Central Av, Palisades Blvd, 11th-19th St; south of 14th (Fort Lee) 17th, 18th, 19th St are today Inwood Terrace, Harvard Place, Glen Road. Anderson Av. One part. Central Boulevard left out (all its junctions 3-4 m off).

sheet-81-1.description: The upper part of an additional sheet of September 1923, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the area west of Broad Avenue on the Ridgefield and Palisades Park line. The part is turned so that north points to the upper right. Grand Avenue crosses the top of the part and Broad Avenue the bottom; between them Maple Avenue, Columbia Avenue, Ruby Avenue, Edsall Avenue, Harwood Avenue and Homestead Avenue run up the page, slightly fanned, with the short stubs of Fairview Street and Prospect Street at the top right. The Ridgefield and Palisades Park boundary line runs between Maple and Columbia Avenues. The blocks east of Columbia Avenue are laid out in long rows of narrow lots, mostly vacant, with scattered frame dwellings; a large range of greenhouses stands between Ruby and Edsall Avenues. The large block 183 between Maple and Columbia Avenues is almost empty, holding one house with outbuildings, and the west side of Maple Avenue is lined with a row of detached dwellings. Brick stores and a gasoline tank stand at the corner of Broad and Columbia Avenues, and a narrow strip between Broad Avenue and the heavy dividing line shows the end of Columbia Boulevard. Water pipes, including a twenty-four inch main along Grand Avenue, are drawn along the streets. A heavy line below Broad Avenue separates this part from the lower part of the sheet, which is drawn at a different orientation.
notes: Columbia, Ruby, Edsall, Harwood and Homestead Avenues west of Broad Avenue carry a West prefix today (West Columbia Avenue and so on).

Only 9 junctions were found and the fitted scale (3.88 px/ft) is about 3 percent below the other 100 ft sheets; Broad Avenue / Columbia Avenue was not detected because the west side of Columbia Avenue is open land.
Printed note: part of this territory formerly shown on Sheets 46, 71, 74, 75 and 76.

Ridgefield, Palisades Park and Leonia, Sheet 81, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line below Broad Av: part 1 (Broad to Grand Av, Maple to Homestead Av, north arrow about +62 deg), part 2 (N. Sylvan Av to Leonia Av between Grand and Broad, Leonia, turned about -38 deg). Part 2: Grand Avenue and Sylvan Avenue left out (residuals 4-7 m; two Sylvan nodes 36 m apart).

sheet-81-2.description: The lower part of an additional sheet of September 1923, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the southern edge of Leonia between Grand Avenue and Broad Avenue, below a heavy dividing line. The part is turned so that north points to the upper left, at a different angle from the upper part of the sheet. North Sylvan Avenue runs along the top of the part, followed by Ames Avenue, Moore Avenue and, at the bottom, Leonia Avenue, which is lettered as the boundary between Leonia and Palisade Park. Grand Avenue runs diagonally down the left side and Broad Avenue down the right, with Elm crossing the middle between Ames and Moore Avenues, and the stubs of Lawn Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Orchard Avenue continuing south of Leonia Avenue. Sylvan Avenue, Moore Avenue and Oakdene Avenue are lettered on the far side of Broad Avenue. The blocks between North Sylvan and Ames Avenues are closely built with a row of two-storey frame dwellings and garages on both frontages, and the block between Ames and Moore Avenues is lined with dwellings on its north side. South of Moore Avenue the large block 43 is mostly open, with a few houses and outbuildings. The rest of the part is laid out in deep vacant lots.
notes: Leonia Avenue is Oakdene Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Grand Avenue was left out of the control: all its junctions were 4 to 7 m from the fit of the others, so Grand Avenue appears displaced against its 1923 line here.
Sylvan Avenue was left out: OpenStreetMap has two Sylvan Avenue nodes 36 m apart at Broad Avenue, and North Sylvan Avenue at the top of the part is cut by the dividing line.
Placed from 6 junctions along Broad Avenue and Leonia Avenue only; positions towards Grand Avenue are extrapolated.

Ridgefield, Palisades Park and Leonia, Sheet 81, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line below Broad Av: part 1 (Broad to Grand Av, Maple to Homestead Av, north arrow about +62 deg), part 2 (N. Sylvan Av to Leonia Av between Grand and Broad, Leonia, turned about -38 deg). Part 2: Grand Avenue and Sylvan Avenue left out (residuals 4-7 m; two Sylvan nodes 36 m apart).

sheet-82.description: An additional sheet of September 1923, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the northern edge of Leonia up to the boundary line with the City of Englewood, which runs across the top of the sheet beneath a note referring to the map of Englewood. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. Grand Avenue runs diagonally down the left side and Broad Avenue down the right; between them Lakeview Avenue, Longview Avenue, Overbrook Avenue, Van Orden Avenue, Vreeland Avenue, Christie Heights and Harrison cross the sheet, and Brook Terrace, Hillcrest Avenue, Eastview Avenue and Kingsley run between them. Lowe runs along the left edge beyond Grand Avenue. Much of the middle of the sheet is the subdivision lettered Christie Heights Realty Company, with long rows of narrow lots that are still largely vacant, and a large open block 12 between Grand Avenue and Hillcrest Avenue holds only a few houses and a dilapidated building. The largest building is Leonia High School, a brick building with an auditorium, manual training and domestic science rooms, standing at the corner of Christie Heights and Broad Avenue beside a large athletic field. Frame dwellings are scattered along Lakeview Avenue, Brook Terrace, Vreeland Avenue and Christie Heights, and in the blocks between Christie Heights and Harrison. The strip beyond Broad Avenue is lettered as part of the Englewood Field golf links. Water pipes, including a twenty-four inch main along Grand Avenue, are drawn along the streets.
notes: Christie Heights, Kingsley and Harrison are Christie Heights Street, Kingsley Street and Harrison Street in OpenStreetMap; Overbrook Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Harrison / Kingsley was rejected (10.5 m from the fit).
Leonia High School and its athletic field occupy block 1 between Vreeland Avenue and Christie Heights.

Leonia, Sheet 82, 100 ft. Grand, Broad, Lakeview, Longview, Brook Ter, Hillcrest, Eastview, Overbrook, Van Orden, Vreeland, Christie Heights, Kingsley, Harrison, Lowe; Leonia High School; Englewood boundary at top. One part.
